## The security review — Peter's instruction, six lenses, two doors closed, the chain OWED

_Superseded on 2026-09-05 by the section above: every row below that reads half done, not
done, recorded-not-done or owed was done and proved there._

Peter, reading the sweeper session's report on 2026-09-04: _"I feel this is a security risk.
Follow the documents and watch the security; nothing may slip through because of decisions
that made things easier but opened a door for hackers."_ The answer was a read-only fleet
(run `wf_f7bd0375-a84`): six reviewers, one lens each — the sweeper's identity and the
escape hatch, the public PUT, the session lifecycle, authorization and audience, the job
and deployment story, and the pack's demands checked one by one — followed by one skeptic
per finding above `low`, instructed to refute. **26 candidates; 14 verified; 11 real, 3
refuted.** The full output is in the run's `journal.jsonl`; the summary is here.

### The sweeper's own decisions: sound

Every lens that touched the sweeper kept it. The service context cannot be minted from a
request (`createServiceContext` has one caller, the sweeper); the nil UUID reaches no
grant that compares user ids, because every such comparison runs on a `Principal` built
from a membership row, which a service context never is; `audit_events.actor_user_id` is a
foreign key to `users`, so an audit write under the sentinel that forgot `actorUserId: null`
would roll the release back rather than record a phantom actor; `UPLOAD_SESSION_SWEEPER` is
resolved by `sweep.ts` alone and no controller injects it; the bootstrap read returns
organization ids and nothing else, is allowlisted to one table, and its guard event carries
a redacted shape with no bound value. `25` §6 and §10 hold on every line of the slice.

### What was real, and what was done

| Finding (severity as verified)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Done                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **High.** A size-mismatched completion left a real, uncounted, undeletable object: the filesystem driver renamed the assembled file into place and _then_ reported its size, and the service's mismatch check released the reservation over an object nothing could delete (`ObjectStore` has no delete). Deterministic quota bypass for anyone holding `file.upload`                                                                                                          | **Fixed, `d4e4398`.** The declaration travels in `BeginMultipartInput.declaredBytes` and the manifest (version 3). `completeMultipart` refuses with the new `SizeMismatchError` _before_ the rename; parts and manifest stay, as for an etag mismatch. The fake refuses the same way. `FilesService` maps it to the existing 422 `size_mismatch` and fails the session. Storage unit case: the mismatch is refused and `objects/` stays empty (reversal named: move the check after the rename)                                                                                                                                                    |
| **Medium.** A one-byte reservation held a full part on disk: `putPart` capped a body at the part size alone                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | **Fixed, `d4e4398`.** `partCeiling`: a part may carry no more than the declaration leaves for its position. Two storage unit cases (the one-byte upload refuses two bytes and accepts one; the last part is capped at the remainder)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| **High.** The octet-stream parser buffered up to a part size per connection _before_ anyone looked at the token — an anonymous caller, no account, could hold the API's memory with a forged token and a slow body                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | **Fixed, `4f29167`.** `createPartAdmission` in `@tmanage/storage` (the same key derivation and verifier the sink uses); the adapter consults it before attaching a data listener, and a body behind a token that does not verify is handed to the handler as zero bytes, which the sink refuses with the same 404. With no local transport the route reads no body at all. Unit suite `fastify-adapter.test.ts` (3 cases: valid reads 40 bytes; forged, expired, wrong-part, missing and part-0 read 0; 413 still after the token). Transport suite: a forged token over the slack is now 404, not 413 — it no longer learns that a ceiling exists |
| **Medium.** `RATE_LIMIT_*` is configured and consumed by nothing; the public PUT has no limit                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | **Half done, `f9ad5e6`.** `createFixedWindowLimiter` (bounded map, oldest key evicted) written and unit-tested, **not wired**. Next: an `admitClient` option on the adapter consulted before the token (429 `rate_limited`), built in `main.ts` from the two env values                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| **Medium.** No cap on open reservations per person: a client reviewer with `file.upload` can open one-byte sessions without end, each a provider upload and a directory                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | **Not done; designed.** `UPLOAD_MAX_OPEN_SESSIONS_PER_USER` (default 20) on the env and `ApiConfig`; `UploadSessionsRepository.countReservedFor`; checked before the provider call and again inside the reservation transaction; refused 429 `rate_limited` with an `upload_session.refused` denial row (`too_many_open_uploads`); the FILE-001 suite gets a cap of 12 and one case                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| **Medium.** The complete/cancel race (carried) — a completion still talking to the provider when a cancel, or now a sweep, moves the row                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | Carried, unchanged. The fix is a claim on the row (`reserved → completing`) before the provider call                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| **Low, real.** `DATABASE_URL === DATABASE_MIGRATION_URL` compares strings, so one credential with a query-string difference passes; the worker reads `DATABASE_URL`, so the least-privilege `tmanage_worker` user is never used; a mysql2 error carries `sql` with bound values inlined and reaches the operator log; abort failures on the create and expiry paths leave provider uploads nobody names; `expire` checks nothing about the row's organization before the abort | Recorded, not done. In order: compare parsed usernames; a `WORKER_DATABASE_URL`; strip `sql` in `unwrapQueryError` and log fields in the sweeper; an audit row naming the handle when an abort fails; one line at the top of `expire`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |

Refuted by the skeptic and dropped: the internal request-attachment audience shape (real,
already recorded as FILE-003's, no read path exists); the absent malware scan and hash
(FILE-002's, no download path exists); the client door's audience rule on a shared project
(same). Deferred, named, not slipped.

## USAGE-001 slice 1 — the plan refuted, then the expiry sweeper built and proved

The sweeper session of 2026-09-04 opened on a green chain and nothing owed, and took the
plan below in the order the record asked: refute first, build second. Four read-only
skeptics (run `wf_b8110818-1cd`, one each for the sweeper's mechanics, its drive and tests,
the pack and the later slices, and the record and the ten questions) re-read every cited
line of the planner's output. **47 refutations, 33 of them wrong line numbers** — the
planner's `files.service.ts` cites are two lines high throughout, its `outbox.ts` cites name
a banner comment and a closing brace, and every `implementation-status.md` cite points at a
different section than claimed (the discarded-boolean row is :1191, decision 11 is
:816-824, decision 7 is :1207-1210). The plan's shape survived; what did not is below, and
each item changed what was built.

### What the skeptics refuted, and what it changed

| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

A one-minute grace (`sweepCutoff`, `EXPIRY_GRACE_MS`) covers a completion that passed its check just before expiry and is still streaming. ## USAGE-001 planned, not built — the fleet's plan, recorded for the next session

Five read-only agents (four readers — the pack, the code, the background-work infrastructure,
this record — and a planner) over the tree at `6daf54b`, run `wf_7e34c244-c97`, while the
chain ran. The skeptic that was to refute the plan did not run: the session's usage limit
was reached as it started. So what follows is **the planner's output, unrefuted**; the next
session re-reads every cited line before building on it, the way the review-debt session
did for the FILE-001b claims. The full output, with about a hundred `path:line` citations,
is in the run's `journal.jsonl` under the session's `subagents/workflows/wf_7e34c244-c97/`.

### What the pack demands (as read)

- `28` §8: _append-only storage ledger, reconciled counters, atomic byte reservation,
  threshold events_, 8 points, after FILE-001 and AUTHZ-001; ENT-001 depends on it.
- `24` §4: four events — `usage.storage_reserved.v1`, `usage.storage_committed.v1`,
  `usage.storage_released.v1` (all three already registered and produced by FILE-001), and
  `usage.threshold_reached.v1` (_70/85/95/100 crossed with hysteresis_; audit "yes at 100%").
  No JSON schema exists for any `usage.*` event under `contracts/events`.
- `49` §6: the bands — 70 insight, 85 warning and cleanup guidance, 95 persistent warning
  and plan offer, 100 block new reservations and keep reads, downloads, deletion, export,
  billing and plan change; and the eight-step atomic reservation algorithm, of which step 7
  (_failure, abort or expiry releases reserved bytes and removes abandoned parts_) is the
  sweeper. **No numeric hysteresis appears anywhere in the pack.**
- `49` §5 and the DBML (`contracts/tmanage-core.dbml` `usage_ledger_entries`): the ledger's
  minimum fields — organization, project when applicable, asset/version, storage class, byte
  delta, reason, source event, occurred time, idempotency key — and a scheduled
  reconciliation against provider inventory.

### The five slices, in order

1. **The expiry sweeper.** Hosted in `apps/api`, not the worker (the worker has no storage
   driver and no `UPDATE` grant on `upload_sessions`; `FilesService.releaseAs` already does
   the whole release atomically and emits `usage.storage_released.v1` with cause `expired`).
   Selection in two steps because `TenantContext` binds one organization and the index
   `ix_upload_sessions_org_status_expires` is organization-prefixed: a `bootstrapRead` for
   the distinct organizations holding `reserved` rows past `expires_at`, then per
   organization a service context and a new `UploadSessionsRepository.listExpired` in
   batches of 100 until a pass releases nothing. Release through the existing
   `releaseAs(…, 'expired', 'best-effort')`; the conditional transition is the idempotency
   gate, so a row moved by complete, cancel or another pass is counted `skipped`. The
   discarded `counters.release` boolean becomes load-bearing: captured into audit metadata
   as `counter_drift`, not thrown. One audit action, `upload_session.expired`, actor null.
   Driven like the relay: `apps/api/src/sweep.ts` with `--once`, a `sweep:once` script, a
   parseable `[sweeper] pass: scanned N, released N, skipped N, failed N` line, and an e2e
   `sweepUploads` beside `drainOutbox`. No new event type. Six database cases and one
   journey (E2E-12b: an abandoned upload is released and the quota is free again).
2. **The append-only ledger**, written in the producing transaction after the outbox row
   (whose id is `source_event_id`): migration `0018_usage_ledger_entries.sql` (0017 was
   taken by the completing claim on 2026-09-05), a `BEFORE
UPDATE` trigger and no `UPDATE`/`DELETE` grant, idempotency key
   `<uploadSessionId>:<reason>`, `INSERT … ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE id = id`. Cases: one
   ledger row per counter move joined to its outbox row; the ledger sums to the counter
   after a mixed sequence including an expiry; a replayed key inserts nothing; rows are
   immutable for the app credential; two tenants never mix.
3. **Reconciled counters**: ledger-versus-counter per organization under `FOR UPDATE`,
   `reconciled_at` written (the column exists and nothing writes it), a correcting ledger
   row and an audit row on drift, version-conditional repair (CONC-06). Provider-inventory
   comparison is **not** possible yet: `ObjectStore` has no list or head.
4. **Threshold events** `usage.threshold_reached.v1` with a band state per organization and
   hysteresis; the 100 % band is what the reservation guard already refuses.
5. **The usage read** for the billing screen (`49` §8 wants used, reserved and quota shown).

### Ten questions for Peter, with the planner's recommendation

1. The sweeper's identity: `createTenantContext` demands a user id and a membership id and
   `principalKind: 'service'` has no builder. Recommend a documented nil-UUID sentinel with
   audit rows carrying a null actor; `25` §10 (background jobs run with scoped repositories)
   is satisfied either way.
2. Using `bootstrapRead` for a job's cross-tenant scan — a new use of the escape hatch,
   documented today for pre-context session resolution. Recommend yes, with an explicit
   reason string.
3. A `false` from `counters.release` or `commit`: record `counter_drift` and proceed, so a
   drifted organization's sessions still expire; slice 3 repairs. The alternative leaves them
   stuck.
4. One audit row per expired session (`upload_session.expired`). Recommend yes: it is the
   only trace of a leaver's abandoned reservation being cleaned (decision 7).
5. The hysteresis value: recommend 5 percentage points below the band. Nothing in the pack
   says.
6. The band's basis: used + reserved (what the guard blocks on) or used alone (what the bill
   measures). Recommend used + reserved.
7. Which capability authorizes the usage read and the threshold notification (AUTH-16). None
   exists in code; ENT-001 may own it. Slices 4 and 5 cannot ship without a name.
8. The ledger's shape: an extra `counter` column (`used` | `reserved`) or two rows per
   commit. Recommend the column, recorded as a divergence; `13-ENGINEERING-EXECUTION-SPEC` (the planner cites line 36) says paid-beta additions
   must not change the P0 ledger contract, so this is Peter's.
9. Provider-inventory reconciliation (QUOTA-07) needs an `ObjectStore` inventory method that
   does not exist. Recommend ledger-only reconciliation in slice 3 and a follow-up.
10. Cadence on the Hostinger target: the same external tick that runs `relay:once` runs
    `sweep:once` after it. No scheduler inside the process.

Slice 1 is buildable now under recommendations 1–4 and 10, each behind one clearly named
function so a different answer is one edit. Nothing was written to the tree for it.

## The queue names its clients by id, and a pressed button is painted — two standing lines closed

The session of 2026-09-04 that followed the review-debt session opened on a green chain and
nothing owed, and took the two smallest standing lines first, in the order the record listed
them. Both are pre-existing, both were named by the chain-first session's fleet, and each is
proved by reverting.

### What was built

| Line                                                  | Done                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ClientRequestsService.list` names from a capped page | `clientOrganizationNames` reads by id through `ClientOrganizationsRepository.findManyByIds` — the ids on the page's own rows — instead of a page of active organizations capped at 200. It is the same helper `getMany` was moved to on 2026-09-03, so the queue now answers what `get` answers: an archived client's request still names its client, and a tenant with more clients than one page holds names every one. Still one read per page. Case, in the inbox suite beside `getMany`'s: submit, archive the client by SQL, `list` carries the same name `get` does |
| `is-active` on the three inbox screens' mode buttons  | The class matched no rule, so the selected mode had no visual state. The hook is now the attribute the screens already set: `.tm-button[aria-pressed='true']` in `packages/ui` paints the toggle as the ink button, whatever its tone, with the ink hover; the inert class is removed from `InboxScreen`, `RequestInboxScreen` and `ClientInboxScreen`. The `States` story shows a pressed and an unpressed outline button, so the VR harness pins the paint; a unit case pins that `aria-pressed` passes through `Button` and the pair is axe-clean                       |

One decision, small enough to state here rather than number: **a pressed toggle is painted
ink, not lime.** Lime is the one call to action on a screen (`40-DESIGN-SYSTEM`), and a mode
toggle is not that; the ink fill is what reads as "this one" beside its outline siblings in
both themes. The attribute rather than a class is deliberate — the state cannot be painted
without being announced.

## FILE-001b, the review acted on — twenty-three claims re-read, nineteen fixed and proved

The session of 2026-09-04 opened on the two debts the review session left: the chain on the
final tree, and the fleet's findings, recorded and untouched. The chain ran first, green.
Then every kept claim was re-read in the source before anything was written — all
twenty-three stand as the skeptic described them; not one was dismissed on re-reading — and
the fixes went in as one batch, each with a case, each case proved red by reverting the fix
it pins. Four claims are recorded rather than fixed, as the review said they should be.

### What each claim became

| #   | Done                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| --- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1   | **Fixed.** The octet-stream parser is now streaming and refuses first: it reads the URL before a byte of the body, answers 415 to any registered route that is not `PUT /v1/uploads/:handle/parts/:n` with the body unread, lets an unrouted URL through untouched to Fastify's own 404, and buffers only the part route, up to its own limit, counting as it goes. `main.ts` still registers it for every driver; on `s3` it costs one URL check and buffers nothing. The helper's header now says what it does. Case: an octet-stream body on `POST /upload-sessions`, 8 bytes and a byte over the parser's limit, both 415 with no detail |
| 2   | **Fixed.** The filter's `part_too_large` envelope is keyed on the request URL matching the part route; every other 413 gets the generic envelope. Case: a 1.1 MB JSON body on `POST /upload-sessions` — 413, `validation_failed`, "The request could not be understood", no `details`. Decision 9 corrected below                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| 3   | **Fixed.** `writeAtomically` writes to `<path>.<12 hex>.tmp` and removes it if the write or the rename fails. Cases: a directory squatting on `part-0001` makes the rename fail and nothing but the manifest remains; two PUTs of one part at once both land whole, each answered the etag of its own body                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| 4   | **Fixed.** Completion is one pass: each part is MD5-hashed and counted through a `Transform` **while** it streams into the staging file, and compared to its presented etag before the next part is read; the size and etag recorded are of the bytes written. Proved by reading; the interleaving it closes cannot be scheduled from a test                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| 5   | **Half fixed.** The staging file is `object.<16 hex>.tmp`, per call, and a refused completion discards it and keeps the parts (case: after a wrong etag, exactly the manifest and the parts remain, and the second completion succeeds). The other half — a claim on the row (`reserved → completing`) before the provider call — is **not done** and stays on the carried list as the complete/cancel race                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| 6   | **Fixed.** `toView` takes the principal; `uploadUrls` is served only when the row is `reserved` **and** the caller opened it. Case, in the wide-list test: the owner's organization-wide list carries `[]` for both sessions while the opener's own read still carries the target                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |

### Decision 11, for Peter to overturn

11. **A refused completion keeps the upload.** On `MissingPartError` or `PartEtagMismatchError`
    the session stays `reserved`, the bytes stay counted, the driver keeps its staging
    directory, and the client re-PUTs the part and completes again. S3 leaves a multipart
    upload intact on `InvalidPart`; a driver that discarded thirteen parts over one mistyped
    etag would be stricter than the provider it stands in for, and the fleet's own plan
    (`releaseAs('failed')` on every refusal) chose that without saying so. Release happens
    only on `MultipartUploadNotFoundError`, when nothing the client does can finish the
    upload; that release's abort is best-effort. Cost: a session refused this way holds its
    reservation until the client completes, cancels, or the expiry sweeper (USAGE-001) runs.

## FILE-001b, parts 2–4 — the bytes move

The session of 2026-09-03/04 (the fifth on the ticket) opened on the two debts the part-1 stop
left — the chain and the storage revert proofs — and then took the fleet's plan through its
last three commits. The API now stands in for the bucket: `main.ts` wires
`FilesystemObjectStore` through `StorageModule.forConfig`, a public `PUT` route receives each
part under an HMAC token the driver minted, and a whole file — two real 8 MiB parts — crossed
HTTP with no cookie, was assembled on disk and became a `file_versions` row. FILE-001 is no
longer half.

### What was built

- **Part 2, `9adb20d` — config and wiring.** `STORAGE_LOCAL_SIGNING_SECRET` is required exactly
  when `STORAGE_DRIVER=filesystem`, placeholder-refused in production and distinct from
  `SESSION_SECRET` and `CSRF_SECRET` across every pair (three credentials with one value are one
  credential). `UPLOAD_PART_SIZE_BYTES` (8 MiB) reaches `FilesService` as
  `ApiConfig.uploadPartSizeBytes`; the constant stays as the default. `StorageModule.forConfig`
  mirrors `MailerModule.forConfig` and provides the driver twice — as `OBJECT_STORE` and as
  `LOCAL_PART_SINK`, which nothing else provides; `s3` still refuses at the first provider call.
  `createFastifyAdapter` registers the `application/octet-stream` parser with **its own** body
  limit (part size + 1 KiB), so Fastify's 1 MiB default stays on every JSON route; `ETag` is
  exposed through CORS. The module header that said "there is deliberately no `forConfig` yet"
  is gone.
- **Part 3, `1b8683a` — the route and the mapping.** `UploadPartsController`:
  `@Controller('v1/uploads') @Public() @NoTenant()`, `PUT :providerUploadId/parts/:n`, a `Buffer`
  body, `?t=` read as a query, no `@Ctx()` and no principal. It authorizes nothing itself; every
  `null` from the driver's `PartSink` is one 404 with one body; a body over the part size is 413
  `validation_failed` (`part_too_large`) whether the driver refused it by one byte or the parser by
  a byte over the slack — the filter maps the parser's 413 to the same detail; a body that names
  another content type is 400, and a body that names **none** — what `fetch` sends for a
  `Blob.slice()` — is Fastify's own 415, not this route's 400 (_corrected 2026-09-04, claim 11;
  pinned by a case_). Success is 200, an empty body, a quoted `ETag`. `FilesService.completeSession` now
  tries `completeMultipart`: `MultipartUploadNotFoundError` / `MissingPartError` /
  `PartEtagMismatchError` fail the session, release the reservation and answer 422 on `parts`
  (`upload_not_found` / `part_missing` / `part_etag_mismatch` as the audit code);
  `MultipartUploadMismatchError` and `UnsafeObjectPathError` stay 500, because both mean this
  service named a zone or key it did not open.
- **Part 4, `d113246` — the journey.** The e2e stack gives the API its own signing secret and
  an absolute, run-private `STORAGE_FILESYSTEM_ROOT` (exported to the specs as
  `TMANAGE_E2E_STORAGE_ROOT`, removed at stop). E2E-12a opens a session for 8 MiB + 16 bytes,
  PUTs both parts from a request context that holds no cookie, completes on the returned etags,
  and finds exactly one `…/object` of the declared size under the tenant's prefix, staging gone.
  Not scan, not download; E2E-12 itself stays unclaimed.

### Decisions the design fleet took — now live, for Peter to overturn

Recorded in the part-1 section as "live when part 2 wires them"; wired now. Restated with what
each cost or bought:

1. **The part URL carries the provider handle**, not the session id, and never the key. The
   handle is a random 128-bit value; the session id is a tenant row id. The transport suite
   asserts neither the organization id nor the session id appears in a URL.
2. **The per-part ceiling is not signed**; it is `UPLOAD_PART_SIZE_BYTES`, read by the service,
   the driver and the parser from one `ApiConfig` number.
3. **Every PUT refusal is one 404 body.** Ten shapes of refusal, one body. Expiry is not
   distinguished — the client already holds `expiresAt` on the session.
4. **Verification lives in the driver**, behind `LOCAL_PART_SINK`; the controller maps `null`.
5. **The manifest is the revocation.** Cancel removes the directory; the outstanding URLs die;
   proved over HTTP, not only in the unit.
6. **Etags are MD5**, hex per part and S3-composite per object, quoted on the wire.
7. **The large body limit is per content-type.** The JSON limit is untouched.
8. **`UPLOAD_PART_SIZE_BYTES` exists so the database suite can drive multipart cheaply** — it
   runs at sixteen bytes, a size no deployment uses; the real 8 MiB is proved once, in E2E-12a.

Two more this session took, in the same spirit:

9. **The parser's own 413 is ours, on the part route only.** _Corrected 2026-09-04 (claim 2
   of the review): as first written this said "any 413 `HttpException` the adapter raises",
   justified by the octet-stream parser being the only limit above the default — but
   Fastify's untouched 1 MiB default on every JSON route is itself a 413 source, so a
   1.2 MiB JSON body against any route answered `exceeds the part size`._ The filter now
   keys the `part_too_large` envelope on the request URL matching
   `/v1/uploads/:handle/parts/:n`; a 413 anywhere else gets the generic envelope
   (`validation_failed`, "The request could not be understood", no detail). Pinned by a
   database case on `POST /upload-sessions` with a 1.1 MB JSON body.
10. **A non-octet-stream body on the part route is 400, not 404.** It is a client bug, and
    saying so reveals nothing about any upload.

### Divergences added to the register

- The size-mismatch orphan (decision 9 of the FILE-001 review) is **no longer latent**: a
  client that PUTs fewer bytes than it declared now materialises a real object under
  `objects/quarantine/` that nothing deletes. Still FILE-003's lifecycle rule (objects with no
  `file_versions` row expire); the port still has no delete, on purpose.
- The route `PUT /v1/uploads/{providerUploadId}/parts/{n}` is not in `openapi.yaml`, and cannot
  be in the shape the contract expects: it is the local substitute for a presigned URL, and the
  contract describes uploads as going to the bucket. Recorded rather than added.
- `27-TEST-CATALOG`: the transport suite's refusal cases (forgery, expiry, replay after cancel
  or complete, a foreign secret) have **no catalog id**; the fleet's proposal to add a
  signed-upload-URL row rather than borrow SEC-01 or AUTH-15 stands, and is Peter's to make.
  The 413 and traversal cases are SEC-06's shape. E2E-12a is a named fraction of E2E-12.

### Carried, unchanged

- **No rate limit on the public PUT.** `rate_limited` is in the vocabulary with no guard; the
  route is bounded only structurally, by the bytes reserved at create and by the token's
  lifetime. A valid token can be re-PUT for fifteen minutes, each write bounded by the part
  size. Recorded for whichever ticket adds the first limiter.
- **The complete/cancel race** (no claim on the row across the provider call) is now observable
  with a real driver and still not fixed; **the expiry sweeper** is USAGE-001's.
- **`s3` wires nothing** until FILE-003 brings R2 signature semantics and bucket CORS.
- **The local transport is a development and e2e path** (_added 2026-09-04, claim 23_).
  `filesystem` is on `packages/config`'s production blacklist, so a production deployment
  names `s3`, `LOCAL_PART_SINK` is never bound, and `PUT /v1/uploads/…` answers 404 to
  everything. Since the review the octet-stream parser refuses every non-part URL by path
  before reading a byte, so the route's parser costs production one URL check per
  octet-stream request and buffers nothing. `.env.example` now says so beside the root.

## FILE-001b, part 1 — the local transport's driver, and a safe stop

After the review session's chain went green and was pushed, a five-agent read-only design
fleet (four lenses — security, wiring, driver, tests — and a proposer; run `wf_57b82325-48f`)
produced a four-commit plan for FILE-001b. The first commit is in: `packages/storage` gains
`FilesystemObjectStore` (ADR-0002's `filesystem` substitute), the HMAC part token, and the
typed errors a driver may answer. **Nothing in `apps/api` uses it yet** — `main.ts` still
passes no store, `StorageModule.forConfig` does not exist, there is no PUT route, and no byte
crosses HTTP. Peter called the safe stop here, at 40% of context, with the package green on
its own.

### What was built

- **The token.** `pu1.{expiresAtMs}.{base64url(HMAC-SHA256)}` over
  `pu1.{providerUploadId}.{partNumber}.{expiresAtMs}`, keyed by
  `HMAC(secret, "tmanage.storage.local-part.v1")`. The handle and the part live in the URL
  path and in the signed input, never in the token; the version label is inside the signature;
  the verifier parses one digits-only integer; signature before expiry; every failure is
  `false`.
- **The driver.** `<root>/uploads/<handle>/manifest.json` and `part-NNNN` while in flight;
  `<root>/objects/<zone>/<object key>` when complete. **The manifest is the revocation**: a
  token cannot be recalled inside its lifetime, the directory can — `abort` removes it and every
  outstanding URL dies; `complete` removes it too. Etags are hex MD5 per part and S3's
  composite per object, so the client side needs no change when FILE-003 swaps drivers. Key
  segments are re-checked against a safe alphabet and the resolved path asserted under the
  zone; a body over `partSizeBytes` is refused after the token and before the write.
- **`PartSink.putPart`** — the half of the driver the public PUT route will call: `null` for
  unknown, forged, foreign, expired, aborted, completed or out-of-range, `{ etag }` otherwise.

### Decisions the design fleet took, for Peter to overturn (recorded now, live when part 2 wires them)

1. The part URL carries the **provider handle** (random 128-bit), not the session id, and
   never the key.
2. The per-part byte ceiling is **not** signed; it is server-side config.
3. **Every** PUT refusal is one 404 body — expiry is not distinguished.
4. Verification lives **in the driver**, behind its own DI token, not in the controller.
5. **The manifest is the revocation.**
6. Etags are **MD5**, S3-shaped.
7. The large body limit will be **per content-type** (`application/octet-stream`), not
   Fastify-global.
8. A new `UPLOAD_PART_SIZE_BYTES` env key so the database suite can drive multipart cheaply;
   the real 8 MiB is proved once, in E2E-12a.

### Decisions added or amended, for Peter to overturn

- **Decision 7, amended.** The person who opened a session reads, completes and cancels it. A
  principal with **organization-wide scope** (the owner) may additionally list every session in
  the studio and cancel a reserved one — never read its parts, never complete it. Without that,
  a reservation only its opener could release was a reservation nobody could.
- **9. Refuse on mismatch.** `49` §6 step 6 says completion verifies the provider's size and
  converts the reservation to used bytes. The slice instead fails the session with 422
  `size_mismatch` when the provider's count differs from the declaration, releasing the bytes;
  it does not meter what arrived. The comment "the provider's count, not the declaration" is
  therefore about which number is compared, not which is stored — by the commit both are equal.
  Metering what arrived would let a caller under-declare to slip past the reservation check.
- **10. A replay is the same upload or a conflict.** Same person, same project, session still
  `reserved`: byte-identical. Otherwise 409, with the reason in `details`.
- **11. `objectId` is mandatory for `request_attachment`, for everyone**, and the request it
  names must be open (not `declined`, `delivered` or `withdrawn`); a closed one is 422
  `request_closed`. `deliverable` and `message_attachment` carry no object yet.
- **12. `uploadUrls` are served only while the session is `reserved`.**

### Divergences added to the register

- `file_versions` is not "the DBML's": the DBML has `content_hash` and `mime_type` NOT NULL;
  0015 has `content_hash` NULL, `declared_mime_type` NOT NULL plus `detected_mime_type` NULL.
  `usage_counters` likewise gains `created_at` and `reconciled_at`. `declared_content_hash` is
  collected and stored and verified by nothing until FILE-002.
- `UploadSession.reservedBytes` is `minimum: 1` in the contract and `0` here once a session has
  left `reserved`. A generated client with response validation would reject the cancel
  response.
- `Idempotency-Key` is `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{16,128}$` here and length-only in the contract.
- `completeUploadSession` requires `Idempotency-Key` in the contract; neither door reads it.
  Completion is idempotent per session, not per key.
- `fileVersionId` is on the 202 and on no read; DEL-001 will need a read that returns it.
- The trust zone is `quarantine` in code and in no column; FILE-002's promotion needs one.
- `usage.storage_committed.v1` carries neither the ledger entry, the effective quota nor the
  threshold band `24` §4 lists; the first and third are USAGE-001's, the second is nobody's yet.
- `upload_sessions` has no `audience`; it is derived from `client_organization_id`.
- 0015's header rests the object key's safety on "`FORBIDDEN_CLIENT_FIELDS` names `storageKey`";
  the correction is in 0016's header rather than in an applied migration.

### Carried to the tickets that make them observable

- **FILE-001b**: the complete/cancel race (no claim on the row across the provider call); the
  signed part URL must carry a session id and a token, never the key; a session past
  `expires_at` still answers its targets to a `GET` until cancel or complete.
- **FILE-002**: etag and content-hash verification; the persisted trust zone; `file_versions`'
  NOT NULL hash.
- **FILE-003**: the orphaned object after a size mismatch (a lifecycle rule for objects with no
  version row); the audience of an internal `request_attachment`, resolved through `object_id`.
- **USAGE-001**: the expiry sweeper (`ix_upload_sessions_org_status_expires` is its index); the
  discarded `commit`/`release` booleans become load-bearing the day it runs. _Built 2026-09-04
  as slice 1 of five — see the sweeper session above; `release`'s answer is now recorded as
  `counter_drift`, `commit`'s is still discarded._

### Ticket accounting

Unchanged: FILE-001 stays at **half**; **33 of 70 tickets, 268 of 583 points (46.0%).** A
review that fixes the slice's own defects earns no points.

## FILE-001 — the upload session, the reservation, and the first file rows

The session of 2026-09-03 (the second that day) took the first line of the standing list:
files, the biggest unblocker. It opened with a six-agent read-only brainstorm over the
planning pack and the repo — five lenses (planning, repo shape, what already existed, tests,
web and design) and a design proposer — which produced three candidate shapes and a
recommendation, and then built the recommended one in three commits, each green on its own.

### What was built

- **`packages/storage`** — the object-store port (`beginMultipart`, `completeMultipart`,
  `abortMultipart`; no download, no delete), the `49-PRICING` §4 key layout built from checked
  UUIDs, and `FakeObjectStore`, which moves no bytes and reports the size a suite configures.
  Modelled one-for-one on `@tmanage/mail`. **No real driver.** `STORAGE_DRIVER` names `s3` and
  `filesystem`, and neither exists; `StorageModule.none()` is `main.ts`'s default and the
  first provider call, not boot, is where a deployment without one fails. ADR-0002 already
  assigns real R2 signature semantics to FILE-003; the local HMAC-signed transport it
  describes is the droppable fourth commit this session did not reach (FILE-001b).
- **Migration 0015** — `usage_counters`, `file_assets`, `file_versions`, `upload_sessions`,
  registered in `TENANT_TABLES`, `schema.ts`'s `TABLES`, `truncateAll` and `users.sql` in one
  commit. Four immutability triggers. `file_versions` is INSERT-only for the runtime
  credential and its trigger refuses UPDATE for every credential.
- **The quota is one statement.** `UsageCountersRepository.reserve` is a conditional UPDATE
  whose predicate is `used + reserved + declared <= limit`; `commit` and `release` guard on
  `reserved >= declared`; both counter columns are `BIGINT UNSIGNED`. No read-then-write
  anywhere. The limit comes from `STORAGE_ORG_BYTES_LIMIT_BYTES` (default 50-BOOTSTRAP §5's
  500 MB) through one seam on `ApiConfig`, for ENT-001 to replace with an entitlement row.
- **`FilesService`** drives `49` §6 with one deliberate reordering: the provider is asked to
  open the multipart upload _before_ the reservation transaction, so no row lock is held
  across a network call; a refused reservation aborts the provider upload. Completion takes
  the provider's size, not the declaration; walks the asset `created → uploading → uploaded`
  through `packages/domain`'s `uploadStateMachine` (its first caller); writes version 1;
  audits `file_asset.uploaded`; appends `upload.completed.v1` and
  `usage.storage_committed.v1`. Cancel, expiry and a size mismatch release, and append
  `usage.storage_released.v1`. Every status move is a conditional UPDATE on the status it
  leaves, so a double complete commits once and a cancel after completion releases nothing.
- **Two doors.** `/upload-sessions` (create, list own, get, complete, cancel) for the studio;
  `/portal/upload-sessions` (create, list own, complete, cancel) for a client attaching to
  their own request, `client_visible` by construction, swept by `ClientProjectionInterceptor`
  and driven through `sec-001`'s §11 grid as its fifth client operation. Each door refuses
  the other kind of principal with 403. `Idempotency-Key` is required; a replay by the same
  person answers the same session byte for byte and reserves nothing; another person's key is
  a 409. The object key is on no response, in no error, and in no audit row.
- **Catalogs.** Four outbox events (`upload.completed.v1`, `usage.storage_reserved.v1`,
  `usage.storage_committed.v1`, `usage.storage_released.v1`), all on aggregate
  `upload_session`; two audit actions (`upload_session.refused`, denied, no object id;
  `file_asset.uploaded`). The worker treats a type with no consumer as delivered, so none of
  these can park the e2e drain.

### Proved by reverting

With the reservation predicate removed from `reserve` (installed from a saved copy, the whole
`file-001-quota` describe run): twelve concurrent reservations against a limit holding ten
were admitted — "expected [...] to have a length of 10 but got 12" — and both refusal cases
flipped. Restored; the file matches the commit. The other rules each name their reversal in
the test that pins them (the `where status = 'reserved'` guard, the `reserved >= ?` guard,
trusting `declared_bytes` at completion, the idempotency unique key, the `UNSIGNED` columns);
those reversals were not run this session and are not claimed.

### Decisions this slice took that no document states

Recorded here for Peter to overturn, each deny-by-default:

1. **Purpose × principal.** Internal: `request_attachment`, `message_attachment`,
   `deliverable`. Client: `request_attachment` only, and `objectId` must name a request of
   their own client organization on the same project. `document`: nobody — Docs is deferred
   past the vertical slice, and an enum member with no live path is the honest state.
2. **A quota refusal wears `validation_failed` (422)** with `auditCode
storage_quota_exhausted`, because `ApiErrorCode` is a closed eight-member set mirrored by
   hand in the web client and `openapi.yaml` declares no non-201 response for
   `createUploadSession` at all. A ninth code is a two-app contract change.
3. **Organization-scoped, not workspace-scoped.** `openapi.yaml`, `49` §5 and `21` all say
   _workspace_; every table in the DBML carries only `organization_id` and `workspaces` holds
   nothing but a name. The counter is keyed on the organization; QUOTA-01's "effective
   workspace quota" is therefore tested against the organization.
4. **`sizeBytes` is capped at `min(UPLOAD_MAX_BYTES, 5 GiB)`** — 50-BOOTSTRAP §5's 100 MB
   wins over the contract's ceiling, which stays as written.
5. **Session and URL lifetime are one value**, `STORAGE_UPLOAD_URL_TTL_SECONDS` (900 s).
   Nothing in the pack gives an upload number; `25` §9's five minutes is for downloads.
6. **A successful upload gets an audit row** (`24` §4 grades `upload.completed.v1` as a
   security log); creating a session does not (`25` §12 does not list it).
7. **Only the person who opened a session may read, complete or cancel it**, on top of
   `authorize()`. An owner sees nothing of a colleague's in-flight upload; the expiry sweep,
   when it exists, is the path that cleans up after a leaver. _Amended by the review session
   (see "FILE-001 reviewed", above): an organization-wide principal may list the studio's
   sessions and cancel a reserved one._
8. **Parts are 8 MiB.** No document bounds `partSizeBytes`.

### Divergences from the planning pack, recorded rather than resolved

- `upload_sessions` exists in `07-DATA-MODEL` and `21` but in no DBML table; the DBML's
  `storage_reservations` carries no name, MIME type, purpose or part size. The two are one
  table here (0015's header).
- `file_assets` as the DBML specifies it lacks `updated_at`, `version`, `project_id`,
  `purpose` and the `(organization_id, id)` key its child needs; 0015 adds all of them.
- `CreateUploadSessionRequest` has no `projectId`; the slice requires one — `49` §6 step 2
  authorizes "the project/object" before reserving and there is no other way to know which.
- `FileAsset` in the contract is `{id, name, status}`; the response is a superset
  (`fileVersionId`, `sizeBytes`, `mimeType`, `purpose`, `projectId`, `versionNo`) because
  `CreateDeliverableVersionRequest` requires `fileVersionIds` no endpoint would otherwise
  return.
- `cancel`, the two reads and the portal list are in no contract; `13` §3 requires cancel.
- Event aggregate is `upload_session`; `24` says `upload`, the DBML `storage_reservation`.
- No JSON schemas were added under `docs/planning/contracts/events/` — that tree is never
  written from a session. The payload interfaces in `packages/domain` are the registered
  shapes until the pack is revised.
- `idempotency_records` stays unused; the session's natural key is the sanctioned
  alternative (`schema.ts`'s message precedent).
- FILE-001 and USAGE-001 are mutually dependent as ticketed (`28` §8); `49` §12 resolves it
  and the slice follows `49`: the counter and the reservation primitive ship here, the
  ledger, thresholds and reconciliation stay USAGE-001's.
- `packages/storage` is not in `18-REPOSITORY-STRUCTURE`'s tree, for `packages/mail`'s reason.

### Named gaps in FILE-001, carried deliberately

- **No bytes move.** `uploadUrls` are `memory://` under the fake and unreachable in a
  deployment; `main.ts` wires no driver. FILE-001b is the local HMAC-signed transport
  (`FilesystemObjectStore`, a `@Public()` PUT authorized solely by the token, `bodyLimit` and
  an octet-stream parser in `main.ts`); FILE-003 the R2 semantics and bucket CORS, which no
  planning document specifies (`ETag` must be in `ExposeHeaders` or the browser cannot
  collect the etags `CompleteUploadRequest` requires).
- **No expiry sweeper.** A session past `expires_at` is released when its owner tries to
  complete it, and otherwise holds its reservation until its opener — or, since the review
  session, an organization-wide principal — cancels it. A scheduled release is USAGE-001's
  lifecycle job.
- **A crash between the provider's completion and the commit transaction** leaves an object
  the database does not know about; a crash between the reservation and the provider's
  `begin` cannot happen (begin runs first) but a crash after `begin` and before the commit
  leaves a provider upload open, which lifecycle-abort (50-BOOTSTRAP §4) is for.
- **`usage.threshold_reached.v1`, the 70/85/95% warnings and the ledger** are USAGE-001.
- **`verifying`, `scanning`, `ready`, `rejected`** are FILE-002's; nothing here writes them,
  and no download exists (FILE-003). A file that is `uploaded` is servable to nobody.
- **`GET /upload-sessions` is not in the role-matrix grid**: the grid drives list-shaped
  GETs through every role and this list is the caller's own sessions, which is a different
  question. Recorded rather than forced.
- **The least-privilege suite has no FILE-001 rows** yet; the grants are exercised only by
  the corpus running green under the app credential where that credential exists (not on the
  default per-file path).
- **WEB-006 is untouched.** No screen, no client module, no query key.

### Ticket accounting

FILE-001 (8 points) is counted **half**: session, multipart shape, quota and both doors are
built and tested; "presigned" is a fake and no byte moves. **33 of 70 tickets, 268 of 583
points (46.0%).**

### One authorized read per object type per page

The first line of the standing list, recorded twice: each bundle's object resolved by its own
`get` or `getForClient`, in sequence, a hundred-odd round trips for a page of a hundred
objects. Now:

- `WorkItemsRepository.findManyByIds` and `ClientRequestsRepository.findManyByIds` — one
  query, the tenant predicate, ids by `IN`. An absent id, or another tenant's, is simply not
  in the result.
- `WorkItemsService.getMany` (same `deletedAt` and `mayRead` as `get`),
  `ClientRequestsService.getMany` (same `mayTriage`, one read for the client organizations'
  names instead of one per row) and `getManyForClient` (same `mayClientRead`, client
  principals only). Each answers a map keyed by id; **what the single read would have refused
  is missing from the map**, which is the 404 without the throw, for a caller that drops the
  bundle silently in every one of those cases and must not learn which.
- `InboxService.bundle` collects the page's ids by object type and resolves them through
  `resolveMany`; `PortalInboxService.bundle` through `getManyForClient`. `markBundleRead`
  still reauthorizes through the single read on both halves — one object, one read.

Proof, on both suites: a case seeds a page of objects a reader can and cannot see — three
readable, one on a project the member is not on, one soft-deleted, one that never existed;
for the client, three of their own, one of a sibling client's, one absent — through a
repository subclass that counts its calls. One `findManyByIds`, zero `findById`, exactly the
readable ones on the page, and every bundle equal field for field to what the single read
answers, while the single read refuses the rest with 404. With the committed services
installed from a copy, all three cases fail — the two new ones on "expected +0 to be 1", and
the portal predicate case, which now watches `getManyForClient` rather than `getForClient`
because that is what the page calls; that repointing is a deliberate change of what the case
pins.

## The client inbox — INBOX-001's second half, E2E-07, and the loop the journey found broken

The session of 2026-09-02/03 (the twenty-fourth) took the first line of the standing list: the
rows NOTIF-001 writes **to clients** — `client_request.transitioned.v1`, to whoever submitted
the request — had no reader, because the internal inbox is guarded by `work.read` and no
client role holds it. Their reader is now a portal projection on a path of its own, the way
every other client surface is; then E2E-07 was built to walk the whole loop through a browser,
and its first run found that the loop had been broken at its first step since REQ-001 landed.

### The client inbox — a projection, not the internal inbox with a filter

`PortalInboxService` (`apps/api/src/modules/inbox/portal-inbox.service.ts`) and
`PortalInboxController` at `/portal/inbox`. The three rules that make the internal half safe
are kept verbatim — **recipient only**, **a bundle is one object**, **the object is resolved
at read time through its own authorized read and a 404 drops the bundle silently** — and the
authorized read here is `ClientRequestsService.getForClient`, which refuses a request outside
the client's own organization and outside the projects shared with it. Four things differ,
each for a reason:

1. **The bundle carries the client's `status`, never the internal `state`.** It is copied from
   `ClientRequestClientView`, whose `status` collapses `triage` into `submitted`; nothing in the
   service ever sees the row. The suite moves a request to `triage` behind the client's back and
   reads `submitted`, and pins the projection's key list so a field cannot arrive by accident.
2. **Only `client_request` rows are read, and the object type is a predicate in the query.** A
   client has no authorized read of a work item by id, so a `work_item` row addressed to a
   client (no consumer writes one today) is never selected. The first cut skipped such rows
   after the read; the fleet found that a skip shortens a page beneath a live cursor, and the
   predicate replaced it. Proved by a case with `limit: 1` and the newest row a work item's.
3. **The event types are allowlisted.** `types` was the one field a row contributed to the
   projection unmapped — an identifier from the internal event catalogue — and both the
   isolation lens and the web lens found it. Only `client_request.transitioned.v1` passes; an
   unknown type is dropped from the list and the bundle stays. The screen says the type in
   words and has no path that prints an identifier.
4. **Two modes, not four**: `all` and `unread`. `important` and `client_actions` are internal
   readings of internal events. **The guard is `client_request.submit`** — the capability that
   put the request in the system reads what became of it — and the service refuses a non-client
   principal again with its own 403, because the owner's and the org_admin's ceilings hold
   every capability and pass the guard. The suite tells the two 403s apart by the guard's
   fingerprint: a `security.capability_denied` audit row for the manager and the member, none
   for the owner and the org_admin (seeded in the suite; the seed world has none).

The screen (`ClientInboxScreen.tsx`, route `/{slug}/portal/inbox`) is modelled on the client
requests list: `aria-pressed` modes, a list of panels, the client-safe status capsule, "Mark
read: {title}", Load more, pages folded by bundle id, "nothing" said only once the cursor is
gone. **The rail was not touched**: `22` §1's client rail has no inbox (`CL-08 Updates` is a
feed of published status updates, which this is not), so the page is reached from `CL-01
Overview` by one link, and the test that the link exists is there because the fleet noticed
that deleting it would strand the feature with every suite green.

### The loop was broken at its first step, and E2E-07 found it

`e2e/setup/stack.ts` boots the API and the web app and not the worker, so no notification row
ever existed in the browser stack. `drainOutbox` runs the worker's own `--once` mode (the shape
the bootstrap profile deploys) with the API's environment, between the act and the assertion;
the database URL crosses into the specs the way the seed world does. E2E-07a then failed on
its first run: a client submitted a request through the portal, the relay ran, and the
studio's inbox stayed empty.

The cause was not the inbox. `ClientsModule` built its `ClientRequestsService` **without the
outbox** — six arguments where `RequestsModule` and `InboxModule` pass seven — and the
service's `append` is optional-chained. So a request submitted or withdrawn **through the
portal** wrote no `client_request.submitted.v1` and no `client_request.transitioned.v1`: no
manager was notified, no mail was composed, and nothing said so. The database suites never
saw it because they construct the service with the outbox and call `submit` directly. Fixed by
injecting `OUTBOX_EVENTS_REPOSITORY` there; pinned by a case that POSTs `/portal/requests` and
withdraws over HTTP and reads the two rows back from `outbox_events`; proved by reverting the
one argument and watching that case fail; and then E2E-07a passed through the browser. The
architecture lens of the fleet found the same defect independently from the argument count.

### E2E-07 — three journeys

`27-TEST-CATALOG` E2E-07: "Notification bundle → inline action: action current-authorized and
devices sync." **E2E-07a**: a client's submission reaches the manager's inbox under "Client
actions" only after the relay runs, with the inline action; marking it read is reauthorized by
the API and a second browser context for the same person sees it read, because read state is
a column. **E2E-07b**: the studio's question reaches the client's inbox with the client's
words and none of the internal ones, their own inline action, and `Unread` empties. **E2E-07c**:
a sibling client's inbox is empty and the studio's inbox refuses a client at the door.

E2E-07b's first run expected one notification and found two, bundled: `submitted → triage`
when the studio opened the request, then `triage → needs_clarification` when it asked. The
consumer notifies the submitter of every transition but their own withdrawal, and `triage` is
a state the client is never shown — so the client is told about a move they cannot see. **A
NOTIF-001 policy question, recorded rather than decided here**: the honest reading of `24` §4
is that "manager inbox, notification" applies to every transition, and silencing one is a
product decision. The journey asserts what the system does.

### The contract, diverged and recorded

`openapi.yaml` draws one `getInbox` and no portal inbox. `GET /portal/inbox` and
`POST /portal/inbox/{bundleId}/read` are not in it; the cursor is `before`; `limit` is
undeclared; `mode` is `all | unread`, not the internal enum; the bundle is
`PortalInboxBundleView`, not `InboxPage.items`. The internal inbox's four divergences stand
beside these. No generated client exists to break.

## The inbox — INBOX-001's first half and the TM-04 screen

The session of 2026-09-02 opened on a stash: "WIP INBOX-001 read surface scaffold, untested".
It was popped (by hand — `git stash pop` refused because `pnpm format` had just rewritten
three CRLF files to LF underneath it; the tracked hunks were applied with `git apply` from
`git stash show -p` and the stash dropped), typechecked clean on the first run, and then
finished: the screen, the route, a web suite and a database suite. One thing in it was wrong
and the database suite found it before any browser did — see "The wiring the stash got wrong".

### What a notification becomes on screen

`22-SCREEN-BY-SCREEN` TM-04: "Tabs: Important, All, Waiting on me, Client actions. Bundles
show count, latest time, required action. Inline actions reauthorize at execution."
`35-NOTIFICATION-AND-EMAIL-COPY` §1: "Access is checked when notification is generated and
again when link/action opens." Four decisions, each a method rather than a sentence:

1. **A row is a reference; the object is resolved at read time, through its own authorized
   read.** `InboxService.bundle` called `WorkItemsService.get` / `ClientRequestsService.get`
   for every bundle — since 2026-09-03 their `getMany`, once per object type per page, see
   "The chain-first session" — and a refusal from either **drops the bundle silently** — no title, no "you
   cannot see this", no count. That is §1's second check and `24-EVENT-CATALOG` §6's "must not
   reveal an object after access was revoked". The database suite proves it three ways: a
   `member` told about work on a project they are not on; a soft-deleted work item; and a
   `member` told about a client request, which they can never read because
   `ClientRequestsService.get` demands `client_request.triage` — the third case was written
   as a _failing_ assertion first (the suite's modes block used the designer and expected the
   request to appear), and the assertion was the thing that was wrong.
2. **A bundle is one object.** Five rows about one work item are one line with a count, the
   unread count, the event types (newest first, each once) and the newest time. The bundle id
   is `objectType:objectId`, and "mark read" takes exactly that — scoped to organization,
   recipient and object, so a person who knows another's object id changes nothing of theirs.
3. **The modes are the planning's words, read literally.** `all`; `waiting_on_me` is what is
   unread (pushed into the query as `read_at IS NULL`); `client_actions` is a bundle carrying
   `client_request.submitted.v1`; `important` is `35` §2's "blocker affecting recipient" — a
   bundle carrying `work_item.blocked.v1`. No ranking and no scoring: `35` §4's "Due today",
   "Blocks 2 people" need facts no row carries and no endpoint computes.
4. **The capability is `work.read`, decided rather than invented.** `12-PERMISSION-MATRIX`
   names no notification capability and NOTIF-001 said the read surface must decide. `work.read`
   is the one capability every internal role holds and no client role does, which is TM-04's
   audience exactly. The role-matrix grid carries the row; a client principal gets the same
   audited 403 as on `/work-items`.

The screen (`InboxScreen.tsx`, route `/{slug}/inbox`) is modelled on `REQ-01`: `aria-pressed`
mode buttons, a table, "Load more" on the cursor. Two deliberate differences. The buttons carry
**no counts**, because a mode here is a different query and a count for a mode not on screen
would be a number the API never gave. And "Mark read" **asks the list again** rather than
editing the row it holds: the API reauthorizes before it writes, and the screen has no way to
know what it decided except by reading.

### The cursor runs backwards

Every other list here pages forward on `after`. An inbox is read newest first, ids are UUIDv7,
so the keyset is `id < before` and a page ends at its oldest row. The contract's `getInbox`
names the parameter `cursor`; the implementation names it `before`, in the same spirit as the
other lists' `after`, and this line records the divergence. Three more, same line: the
contract declares no `limit` and this takes one; it types `bundleId` as a uuid and it is
`objectType:objectId` here, because a bundle is an object and the object type is what tells
the screen where to link; and `POST …/inbox/{bundleId}/read` is not in the contract at all —
TM-04's inline action has an endpoint the contract never drew. A cursor that is not a UUID is
refused with a 400 naming the field, which the two older `after` cursors do not do; recorded
rather than retrofitted.

### The wiring the stash got wrong

The stash's `InboxModule` injected `WORK_ITEMS_SERVICE` and `CLIENT_REQUESTS_SERVICE` from
their modules. Nest refused at boot — the first run of the database suite skipped all fifteen
cases with "Nest can't resolve dependencies of Symbol(tmanage.InboxService)". Those modules are
registered through `.register()` and importing one builds a second copy, controllers and all,
which `ClientsModule` and `ConversationsModule` already document. The fix is theirs: the module
now constructs its own `WorkItemsService` and `ClientRequestsService` from the global handles
(`TENANT_DATABASE`, `AUDIT_SERVICE`, `OUTBOX_EVENTS_REPOSITORY`). Both are stateless over the
same handles, and the inbox only ever calls `get` on them. `typecheck` had passed on the stash;
this is the kind of thing only a booted application finds, which is why the suite boots one.

### Recorded narrowings

- **Bundles split at page boundaries, and the screen folds them.** A page is `limit` rows,
  bundled; an object whose rows straddle two pages appears on both, once per page. The API
  keeps that shape — paging by object is a different query — and the screen merges the two
  appearances by bundle id (a fleet finding; see below). A reader sees one row.
- **A page can still be short, never wrong about the end.** Every mode is a predicate in the
  query (a fleet finding — the first cut filtered two of them after the read), so the only
  thing a page loses after the read is a bundle whose object this person may no longer see.
  Such a page says "nothing you can still see on this page" with the cursor beneath it; the
  absolute "nothing" is said only once the cursor is gone.
- ~~**One authorized read per bundle.**~~ **Closed 2026-09-03** — `WorkItemsService.getMany`
  and `ClientRequestsService.getMany`, one query per object type per page, the same
  `mayRead`/`mayTriage`. See "The chain-first session".
- ~~**Client recipients have no reader yet.**~~ **Closed 2026-09-03** — the portal projection
  above. Until then `client_request.transitioned.v1` rows, written to the client who submitted,
  accumulated unread: fail-closed, nothing leaked.
- ~~**No browser journey.**~~ **Closed 2026-09-03** — `drainOutbox` and E2E-07's three
  journeys, above. The stack still does not run the worker; a journey drains the outbox itself.
- **No design artifact.** `41-WHOLE-APP-SCREEN-AND-STATE-MATRIX` §4 has `IN-01` through
  `IN-05` and no TM-04 row; `docs/design/source` has no inbox artifact, so `audit:design` has
  nothing to check the screen against.
- ~~**The rail's href is still org-less.**~~ **Closed 2026-09-03** — `AppShell` takes the
  slug and prefixes every item, as `ClientPortalShell` has since WEB-004. See "The chain-first
  session".
- **Quiet hours, digests, channel preferences** need a preferences table the contract does
  not draw — NOTIF-001's first named gap, unchanged. **TM-05 bundle detail** is not built; a
  row links straight to its object. **Bulk mark read with an undo interval** is not built; the
  trigger makes a read row permanent.
